reason: κ of 0.6 is where agreement between two raters is usually called substantial rather than moderate. Below it, the judge disagrees with a careful human often enough that a pass rate it reports could move by more than the changes the loop is trying to measure, so its numbers couldn't be trusted to tell a fix from noise. It applies to each judge's pooled row on judge-test, not to the judge-dev labels it was tuned on.
